content: SEC. 3.2 PROPERTIES OF VECTORS AND MATRICES

When an attempt is made to form the product \( BA \), we discover that the dimensions are not compatible in this order because the rows of \( B \) are three-dimensional vectors and the columns of \( A \) are two-dimensional vectors. Hence the dot product of the \( j \)th row of \( B \) and the \( k \)th column of \( A \) is not defined.
If it happens that \( AB = BA \), we say that \( A \) and \( B \) commute. Most often, even when \( AB \) and \( BA \) are both defined, the products are not necessarily the same.

We now discuss how to use matrices to represent a linear system of equations. The linear equations in (3) can be written as a matrix product.
